title: Top 5 UiPath Alternatives Compared in 2026
summary: Compare five UiPath alternatives for browser and desktop workflows, including their strengths, trade-offs, pricing, and migration effort.
body_markdown:
Every UiPath alternative conversation I've had starts one of two ways. Either the renewal quote arrived and finance flinched, or the team spent another sprint fixing bots that broke when a screen moved. Sometimes both.


I’m biased: I built Skyvern. But for[business workflows that run in a browser](https://www.skyvern.com/products) , I think it’s the best UiPath alternative. Its AI agents use computer vision to understand each page, so they can adapt when buttons move or layouts change. That means less time fixing bots and more time automating tasks like[filling forms](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/automate-form-filling-with-skyvern-ai-browser-automation/) and downloading invoices.


With that out of the way, let's dive in!


## 1. Skyvern


[Skyvern](https://www.skyvern.com/) is an[open-source browser automation](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/best-free-open-source-browser-automation-tools-in-2025/) SDK and server (AGPL-3.0, more than 23,000 GitHub stars). It's an AI alternative to UiPath for back office tasks in the browser.


Instead of recording selectors, you describe the task. An agent then[reads each page visually](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/how-skyvern-reads-and-understands-the-web/) and uses LLM reasoning to choose an action. When a portal changes its layout, the agent can adapt by reading the new page, though that doesn't guarantee every run succeeds. A moved button doesn't break the run the way a stale selector would.


What Skyvern does better:


- Works on sites it has never seen, so one workflow covers many portals with no per-site scripting.
- Logs in with credentials from an encrypted vault, or from 1Password, Bitwarden, or Azure Key Vault, with[2FA](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/how-skyvern-handles-authentication/) handled (TOTP, email codes, SMS forwarded through its API).
- Workflows built from about 20 block types, including loops, human-in-the-loop approval, file downloads, and an HTTP request block for your systems.
- Structured JSON extraction against a schema, plus schedules, webhooks, and parallel runs for scale.
- Code caching replays successful runs as deterministic scripts, with the AI agent as fallback when a page changes.


You can use Skyvern through its web interface,[Python/TypeScript SDKs, APIs and MCPs](https://www.skyvern.com/developers) . It's built for teams that want AI-powered automation for everyday business processes.


Trade-offs: Skyvern automates browsers, not desktop apps. See our[RPA vs AI agents guide](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/rpa-ai-agents-comparison-guide/) .


[Cloud pricing](https://www.skyvern.com/pricing) is public: free with 5,000 credits, Hobby at $29/month, Pro at $149/month with residential proxies. Self-hosted deployment works with your own LLM keys, including local models through Ollama.


For a direct feature-by-feature look, check out our[UiPath vs Skyvern comparison](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/uipath-vs-skyvern-review/) .


## 2. Microsoft Power Automate


**Microsoft Power Automate** is Microsoft's workflow automation suite: cloud flows for API work and desktop flows for RPA on Windows, integrated with Microsoft 365. It's the established enterprise option for companies that already run on Microsoft.


What Power Automate does better:


- A low-cost entry point into attended RPA for Microsoft shops. Many Microsoft 365 plans include basic cloud flows with standard connectors. Paid licenses unlock premium and custom connectors. Premium adds attended desktop flows and process mining for individual users.
- Integration with Excel, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Dataverse, where most mid-market business processes run.
- Desktop flows cover Windows UI automation, which pure web tools don't.


Trade-offs: unattended robots mean moving to per-bot licenses, and the agent features are a separate product. Copilot Studio's computer use tool lets an agent work websites and Windows apps from plain-language instructions, on machines you manage in Power Automate. It bills Copilot Credits per step, and credit packs cost $200 per month for 25,000 credits.


All three Power Automate prices are monthly equivalents billed annually. Premium is $15 per user per month. Process, for unattended bots, is $150 per bot per month. Hosted Process, which runs the bot on a Microsoft-hosted machine, is $215 per bot per month. Each of those plans includes standard, premium, and custom connectors.


## 3. Automation Anywhere


**Automation Anywhere** is one of the closest UiPath competitors. Its enterprise platform adds intelligent automation features to RPA and is now marketed as an[Agentic Process Automation](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/apa-vs-rpa-automation/) system. If most of your bots drive desktop apps, it's the one I'd look at first.


What Automation Anywhere does well:


- The same core automation capabilities as UiPath: attended and unattended bots, a Control Room to run them, and recorders for desktop and web apps. Your team's RPA skills carry over, even though the bots get rebuilt.
- Intelligent document processing uses machine learning models, natural language processing, and computer vision to read documents. It turns unstructured data from invoices, forms, contracts, and handwritten notes into structured records.
- Agentic automation features, including AI Agent Studio for low-code agents and a Generative Recorder that falls back to generative AI when a screen changes.
- A cloud-hosted Control Room, with on-premises deployment for teams that need it.


Trade-offs: it's still a full enterprise RPA rollout. Leaving UiPath means rebuilding bots, retraining developers, and setting up orchestration again. Automation Anywhere's own estimate is weeks for a proof of concept and three to six months to reach production scale. Its AI features sit on top of a traditional RPA core, so test the self-healing on your own screens before you count on it.


Pricing is quote-only. If the UiPath renewal is why you're looking, get a quote early, because you'll be negotiating another enterprise contract.


## 4. SS&C Blue Prism


**SS&C Blue Prism** is an established, governance-heavy RPA platform, acquired by SS&C Technologies for about $1.6 billion in 2022. It's designed for regulated organizations, where changes to automated processes need an owner and an audit trail.


What Blue Prism does well:


- A control-room model built for audited, regulated environments: credential separation, release management, and role-based access as first-class ideas.
- Licensing per digital worker, which some finance teams find easier to budget than per-user seats.
- Its AI agents come with an AI gateway that adds guardrails and audit trails to model use.


Trade-offs: it's built for centers of excellence with trained developers. Small automation teams tend to find it slower to ship in than UiPath. Document processing, business process management, and AI agents are listed as separate products, so confirm which of those capabilities your quote includes.


There's no self-serve start. It sells through SS&C's enterprise sales and support motion, quote-only.


## 5. Sema4.ai (formerly Robocorp)


**Sema4.ai** is an enterprise AI agent platform. It grew out of **Robocorp** , an open-source, Python-first UiPath alternative that Sema4.ai acquired in January 2024.


Robocorp's idea was to write bots as ordinary Python instead of drag-and-drop flows. Its open-source library, rpaframework, is still maintained under Apache 2.0. It covers browsers, Windows desktop apps, Excel, PDFs, and email. Sema4.ai now uses the same Python approach for actions, the code its AI agents call to work with your systems.


What it does well:


- Create RPA solutions in ordinary Python, versioned in git and testable in CI
- Targets document-heavy agent work on enterprise data platforms


Trade-offs: you're picking between two different things. The open-source library is free and fully yours, but your engineers run the scheduling, credentials, and monitoring that UiPath's Orchestrator handles today. The Sema4.ai platform adds a Control Room and enterprise observability, plus Agent Studio, where nontechnical users can create and manage agents with natural-language Runbooks. It's sold for AI agent work, so confirm your bot workloads fit before you plan a migration. You'll still need Python developers to maintain Python bots or build custom actions.


## Picking your UiPath alternative


If the business processes you want to automate run in a browser, try Skyvern as your UiPath alternative. For most teams I talk to, that means logging in to vendor portals, filling out the same forms, and[downloading invoices](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/how-to-automate-downloading-invoices-september-2025/) or reports. Bots that mostly drive desktop apps are a different job, and the desktop RPA platforms on this list are built for it.


Skyvern reads the current page and uses AI to choose each browser action. You describe the task in plain language, so you aren't maintaining a selector for every field by hand. When a portal moves a button, the agent can find it by reading the new layout. It also signs in with credentials from an encrypted vault and handles the 2FA step.


[Try Skyvern free](https://app.skyvern.com/?ref=skyvern.com) with a task you repeat every month, like downloading last month's invoices from a vendor portal.
